findings.issue_text: Removing `.panel`’s `float: right` breaks header variants where `.panel` is outside the new flex `.contents` container: `margin-left: auto` has no effect, so the login panel is no longer right-aligned.

goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

per_golden_matches.reasoning: Both comments identify the same core issue: removing the `float: right` from `.panel` breaks the right-alignment of the login panel in certain header variants where the panel is not a flex item (outside the flex container). The golden comment mentions the non-Ember/noscript header where `.panel` is nested inside `.row`, while the candidate mentions cases where `.panel` is outside the new flex `.contents` container. Both correctly identify that `margin-left: auto` won't work in these cases because the element isn't a flex item. The candidate doesn't mention the 'mixing float with flexbox' concern, but it does capture the main layout regression issue.
